purpose: The first named id-space migration (docs/foundation-graph-schema.md §6). It maps the graduation-slice / academy-session id space (source-family-001 …) onto the frozen fnd-* foundation graph, so authored, server-scored assessment items line up with the ontology. It is a translation layer, not a rename: the slice ids are unchanged, so no learner record is re-keyed yet; this makes graph coverage computable and surfaces where the graph has no home for a graduation skill.
authority: NOT authoritative. The pairings and confidences are one reviewer's proposal; educators confirm or correct them during the audit (plan step 5). Do not treat an 'approximate' or 'clear' link as a validated pedagogical claim.

confidenceScale.clear: the graduation skill is essentially the graph move
confidenceScale.approximate: related — a genre-specific instance or a near neighbour of the graph move
confidenceScale.unmapped: no current graph equivalent; a graph audit / expansion candidate

source-family-001.note: recognize the genre/family of a source

citation-001.note: reading a citation as an address is a navigation meta-skill with no graph node

hebrew-anchor-001.note: anchoring on a recognized high-frequency word

repeated-language-001.note: recognizing repetition/emphasis as a signal — no graph signal node for it

tanakh-narrative-command-001.note: narrative-vs-command mode; graph has asking-vs-telling but not this axis

mishnah-case-001.note: identify the case the Mishnah governs

mishnah-ruling-001.note: locate the ruling within the Mishnah

mishnah-dispute-001.note: spotting two positions = naming where readings diverge

gemara-question-001.note: label the line as a question

gemara-answer-001.note: follow the response to the question

halakha-source-ruling-001.note: separate the source text from the derived ruling

halakha-boundary-001.note: a practical boundary is the limit of the rule

midrash-verse-001.note: identify the verse a Midrash cites

midrash-move-001.note: midrashic/aggadic interpretive move — the graph is argument-shaped and under-covers midrash (reduce-Gemara-dominance gap)

tefillah-blessing-001.note: a blessing formula is a fixed liturgical formula

tefillah-prayer-move-001.note: praise/request/thanks is a tefillah-specific move with no graph node

history-canon-order-001.note: ordering the canon by era = placing sources in time

habit-recovery-001.note: study-habit / rhythm, not a reading skill; outside the graph

habit-transfer-001.note: transfer a move to a new source = carry it across genres
